title: Research Mexico residency options
description: Temporary Resident (1-4 years) vs Permanent Resident. Most Americans start with Temporary Resident via economic solvency.

title: Select your Mexican consulate
description: Apply at the consulate with jurisdiction over your US residence. Requirements can vary by consulate - check their specific requirements.

title: Choose Mexico entry city and plan INM office visit
description: After getting your visa sticker, you'll exchange it for a resident card at INM within 30 days of entry. Research INM offices in your destination city.

title: Research cost of living in target Mexican cities
description: CDMX, Guadalajara, Mérida, Puerto Vallarta, San Miguel de Allende, Oaxaca - each has different costs and expat communities.

title: Budget for consulate fees + INM fees + resident card
description: Consulate visa fee, INM processing fee, and resident card fee are all separate. Budget approximately $400-600 USD total.

title: Choose long-term city and housing strategy
description: Many expats do short-term rentals first to explore neighborhoods before committing to a long-term lease.

title: Start learning Spanish
description: While many expat areas have English speakers, Spanish is essential for daily life, bureaucracy, and integration.

title: Passport validity check
description: Ensure passport has at least 6 months validity beyond your intended stay and blank pages for stamps.

title: Prepare financial solvency proof (Option A: Bank Balance)
description: Show bank statements with minimum balance held for 12 consecutive months. Amount varies by consulate but typically around $43,000 USD or more.

title: Prepare financial solvency proof (Option B: Monthly Income)
description: Show proof of regular monthly income for past 6 months. Minimum typically around $2,600 USD/month - check your consulate's specific requirements.

title: Gather bank statements (6-12 months)
description: Original bank statements showing account holder name, account number, and balances. Some consulates require bank letterhead.

title: Gather investment account statements (if applicable)
description: Investment accounts can count toward financial solvency. Get official statements from brokerage.

title: Prepare proof of income (employment letter, pay stubs, tax returns)
description: If using income method, gather W-2s, pay stubs, or employer letter confirming salary.

title: Obtain passport-sized photos (Mexican specifications)
description: Check your consulate's specific photo requirements - size, background color, and format may vary.

title: Complete visa application form
description: Download and complete the visa application form from your consulate's website. Some consulates have online systems.

title: Prepare marriage/birth certificates (if applicable)
description: If applying for family members, gather certified copies with apostilles. May need Spanish translations.

title: Schedule consulate appointment
description: Book appointment at your Mexican consulate. Wait times vary - schedule well in advance.

title: Attend consulate appointment
description: Bring all documents: passport, photos, application form, financial proof. Brief interview is typical.

title: Pay visa fee at consulate
description: Fee is paid at the appointment. Check accepted payment methods (cash, credit card, money order).

title: Receive visa sticker in passport
description: If approved, visa sticker is placed in passport. This is valid for 180 days to enter Mexico and begin residency process.

title: Verify visa details (dates, entries, name spelling)
description: Check all information on the visa sticker for accuracy before leaving the consulate.

title: Book flights to Mexico
description: Enter Mexico within the visa validity period. Your visa sticker is NOT a resident card - you must exchange it at INM within 30 days.

title: Enter Mexico within visa window
description: Present visa sticker at immigration. You'll receive an FMM stamp and have 30 days to complete INM process.

title: Keep your FMM form safe
description: The FMM (tourist card) portion stamped at entry is critical. Do not lose it - needed for INM appointment.

title: Schedule INM appointment for resident card exchange
description: Book 'Canje' appointment at INM within 30 days of entry. This exchanges your visa sticker for actual resident card.

title: Pay INM fees (bank deposit)
description: Pay the INM processing fee at a bank before your appointment. Keep the payment receipt.

title: Attend INM appointment
description: Bring passport, FMM, consulate visa, payment receipt, photos, and proof of address. Fingerprints and photo taken.

title: Receive temporary resident card
description: Card is typically ready for pickup within 2-4 weeks. This is your official Mexican residency document.

title: Get CURP (Mexican ID number)
description: With your resident card, obtain a CURP. This is Mexico's national ID number needed for many services.

title: Consider RFC (tax ID) if planning to work or invoice
description: RFC is Mexico's tax ID. Needed if you'll have Mexican income, open certain accounts, or sign some contracts.

title: Open Mexican bank account
description: With resident card and proof of address, open a bank account. Popular: BBVA, Santander, Banorte, or digital banks.

title: Get Mexican phone number
description: Telcel, AT&T Mexico, or Movistar. Prepaid SIMs available everywhere. Consider postpaid plan once you have bank account.

title: Understand residency renewal schedule
description: Temporary Resident is valid 1-4 years (as granted). Track your expiration date and renewal deadline.

title: Set calendar reminder for renewal (30-60 days before expiry)
description: Begin renewal process before your card expires. Late renewals can complicate your status.

title: Track time toward permanent residency
description: After 4 consecutive years as Temporary Resident, you can apply for Permanent Residency. Maintain continuous residency.

title: Understand Mexican tax obligations
description: If you become a Mexican tax resident (183+ days), you may owe Mexican taxes on worldwide income. Consult a tax professional.

title: Maintain US tax compliance
description: US citizens must file US taxes regardless of residence. Report foreign accounts (FBAR) if balances exceed $10,000.

title: Register with IMSS or get private health insurance
description: IMSS is Mexico's public healthcare system. Private insurance is also widely available and affordable.

title: Document storage and backup system
description: Keep digital and physical copies of resident card, CURP, passport, bank statements, and tax documents.

title: Consider Mexican driver's license
description: US licenses work temporarily but getting a Mexican license simplifies things. Requirements vary by state.
